Q: failed to solve (exit code: 100). Error in docker A:

I was facing the same issue. You need to first upgrade system and then update system and install any package you want.

FROM ubuntu
RUN apt-get upgrade & apt-get update
RUN apt-get install python3 -y

This will resolve the issue.

Q: Pandas rolling window over a time period if some data might be missing within groups A:

Even your loop solution seems to be wrong. You can easily prove that calculating mean for last row, the 25/07/2025 Group 2 you have added. Taking values of subset for (Weekday == 4) and (Group == "Group 2") and (Date > Date - "21D") (pseudo code) you end up calculating mean of 7 and 5 which is 6, and your code outputs 4.5.

My solutions uses double .groupby and .rolling with date offset. I did few manual validations and output records seem correct.

Idea is to:

  1. Format date column and make it index as date offsets are only valid for datetimelike indexes.
  2. Group by Group and Weekday, then calculate rolling average using 3 week time offset, saving results to new data frame.
  3. Merge two data frames on Date and Group.
  4. Turn Group, Date and Weekday indexes back to columns.

Using 21D date offset makes sure that output is always calculated for last 3 weeks, whether there is missing data or not.

Note that my solution is always giving a output per row, even if there is less that three records taken into evaluation. If this behavior is undesired I can adjust the solution to put NaNs instead.

# Format date column
df["Date"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Date"])

# Set date as index
df = df.set_index(["Date"])

# Rolling mean saved in new df_avg due to index diff with df
df_avg = pd.DataFrame()
df_avg[["Data 1 L3W Av", "Data 2 L3W Av"]] = (
    df.groupby(["Group", "Weekday"])[["Data 1", "Data 2"]].rolling("21D").mean()
)

# Left join df_avg to df on Group and Date and Weekday
df = df.set_index(["Group"], append=True).join(df_avg)

# Drop redundant "Weekday" column, turn "Group", "Date" and "Weekday" indexes back to columns
df = df.drop(columns="Weekday").reset_index()

I have simplified this solution, following @wjandrea suggestions.

Q: Why is freeze panes causing error 1004 when workbook is minimized? A:

Tests with "Application.ScreenUpdating = False" or "Windows("TestNew).Visible = True" did not solve the problem.

After maximizing the WB, it worked well.


    Workbooks("TestNew").Sheets(1).Activate
     
    Set WbShP = Workbooks("TestPrevious").Sheets(1)
    Set WbShN = Workbooks("TestNew").Sheets(1)
    
    Windows("TestNew").WindowState = xlMaximized 'maximize Excel
    Windows("TestNew").WindowState = xlMaximized 'maximize the workbook in Excel

    WbShN.Cells(rowA8_Start, 1).Select
    ActiveWindow.FreezePanes = True

Q: What is the most memory-efficient UI artefact to display a "Critical Out of Memory (OOM)" alert in Android? A:

Is it worth worrying about this? On most Android's they will be running the Low memory Killer Daemon and your process will be killed without the chance to display anything before you get to Out Of Memory situation.

Q: How to modify someone else's Github pull request? A:

UPDATE! (there's an easier way now!)

Imagine the PR ID is 12. Simply run this:

git fetch origin pull/12/head:pr-12

This fetches PR #12 into a new local branch named pr-12

git switch pr-12

This switches to the branch.

Make changhes, push 'em back.

OLD METHOD THAT STILL WORKS

Step 1: in your local repo add a new remote pointing to contributor's

git remote add contributor https://github.com/contributor/repo.git

You will now have two remotes - origin and conritbutor. To verify - run this: git remote -v

Step 2: fetch from new remote

git fetch contributor

Step 3: create a new branch from their changes

git checkout -b contributor-main contributor/main

(replace "main" with "master" if needed)

Step 4: Make changes, commit and push

git push contributor contributor-main:main

If the contributor has "allowed changes form maintainers" when creating the PR (most do b/c it's the default option), the new commit will show up in the PR instantly

P.S. Replace "contributor" with the user's name
